nodes.statement: Every unit-diameter subset of R^6 is contained in a ball of radius r=sqrt(3/7).
After choosing a point c of the set on the enclosing r-sphere, the set lies in L=B_r(0)∩B_1(c), |c|=r.
For 0<delta<r and h=sqrt(r^2-delta^2/4), the top cap above x6=h has diameter at most delta.
The remainder is split by x1=...=x5=0 into 32 sign sectors.
Each sector has diameter squared at most 2r^2+2h ell<1, ell=1/(2r)-r.
The two lens spheres intersect in x6=-ell with horizontal radius rho, rho^2=5/12.
Each sector has an interior intersection-sphere point at exact distance 1 from c in the cap.
Any two distinct sectors contain strict-interior intersection-sphere witnesses with squared distance at least 15/13.
The incompatibility graph of the 33 Lassak atoms is K_33.
No coarsening by unions of whole Lassak atoms can use <=32 strict-diameter parts.
Unit-distance parallel cuts preserve UCS coverage.
R4 uses orthogonal centered slabs; the project-local lemma generalizes to m-1 orthogonal slabs in R^m.
In the R4 three-dimensional projection, rhombic-dodecahedron normals and symmetry reduce truncations to four UCS representatives.
4D cube directions/facets define eight cone parts; the combinatorial construction extends to 6D as 64 directions/12 facets.
For every orientation, a center-apex untruncated R6 facet cone has two lens boundary points at squared distance 10/7.
A new five-dimensional truncation/orbit system and strict R6 diameter certificate are required to escape the frozen Lassak template.
